Entry Response Explanations 

![](/static/whiteBullet.gif) Entry Response Explanations

uploadEntry responses

If everything goes correctly, the system will respond with the following:

<accepted>
	<entry-no>ABC-0000001-1</entry-no>
</accepted>

  
This, however does not mean the entry was accepted by customs. It only states that the entry has been successfully uploaded into the system.

If you include the <transmit> tag, the response will also include the following:

<accepted>
	<transmitted />
	<entry-no>ABC-0000001-1</entry-no>
</accepted>

  
or:

<accepted>
	<not-transmitted>entry contains errors</not-transmitted>
	<entry-no>ABC-0000001-1</entry-no>
</accepted>

  
An accepted entry may also include warnings. They would be returned as follows:

<accepted>
	<warning>Warning message appears here</warning>
	<entry-no>ABC-0000001-1</entry-no>
</accepted>

  
For Type 86 entries, additional warnings have been added to help assist brokers to be compliant with CBP regulations. The following checks have been put into place:  
1\. If a description is used that matches our internal list of generic descriptions, we will give a warning to update the description to be more specific. (e.g. Items would be a generic description that CBP might flag)  
2\. If a description is used for multiple different HTS codes in the upload, our system will throw a warning to make each tariff have a unique description.  
3\. Each tariff needs a description. If there is not one, the system will throw a warning to inform the user.  
4\. Chapter 98 tariffs are invalid for type 86 entries.  
5\. The consignee name will be checked against a list of invalid consignees provided by CBP.  
6\. Check if the weight to value ratio (weight per kilogram / value in dollars) is greater than 1.  
7\. Check to see if the preparer port is required or invalid  
  
These warnings could be configured to "Informational", "Error", or "None" under Account -> Preferences -> Broker Preferences.  
1\. Information - The system will create the entry and provide the warnings as shown in the example below  
2\. Error - The system will not create the entry and provide the cbp-warnings inside a <rejection> tag  
3\. None - The system will not check for these warnings at all.  
  
The system will report these errors in the <cbp-warning> tag as a direct child of the <accepted> tag. The below is an example with the "Informational CBP Warnings" setting and the Entry Number in the request.  

<accepted>
  <warning>Existing warning message appears here</warning>
  <entry-no>ABC-0000001-1</entry-no>
  <cbp-warnings>
    <entity-warning>
      <entity-type>ENTRY\_NUMBER</entity-type>
      <entity-id>ABC-0000001-1</entity-type>
      <warning>
        <type>hts-duplicate-description</type>
        <description>Multiple HTS cannot contain same Description</description>
        <invalid-item>HATS</invalid-item>
      </warning>
      <warning>
        <type>hts-generic-description</type>
        <description>HTS has a generic Description</description>
        <invalid-item>ITEMS</invalid-item>
      </warning>
      <warning>
        <type>hts-value-ratio</type>
        <description>
          The Value to Weight ratio must not exceed 1.0 KG per dollar
        </description>
        <invalid-item>220.0</invalid-item>
      </warning>
      <warning>
        <type>invalid-consignee</type>
        <description>The consignee is invalid</description>
        <invalid-item>CRAZY GRANDMA</invalid-item>
      </warning>
      <warning>
        <type>preparer-port</type>
        <description>The Preparer Port is Required</description>
        <invalid-item></invalid-item>
      </warning>
    </entity-warning>
  </cbp-warnings>
</accepted>

An example with the "Error CBP Warnings" setting and with the system genenerated entry number in request
<rejected>
  <cbp-warnings>
    <entity-warning>
      <entity-type>INVOICE\_NUMBER</entity-type>
      <entity-id>12345</entity-type>
      <warning>
        <type>hts-duplicate-description</type>
        <description>Multiple HTS cannot contain same Description</description>
        <invalid-item>HATS</invalid-item>
      </warning>
      <warning>
        <type>hts-generic-description</type>
        <description>HTS has a generic Description</description>
        <invalid-item>ITEMS</invalid-item>
      </warning>
    </entity-warning>
    <entity-warning>
      <entity-type>NO\_ID</entity-type>
      <entity-id></entity-type>
      <warning>
        <type>invalid-consignee</type>
        <description>The consignee is invalid</description>
        <invalid-item>CRAZY GRANDMA</invalid-item>
      </warning>
      <warning>
        <type>preparer-port</type>
        <description>The Preparer Port Should match the Account Processing Port</description>
        <invalid-item>3001</invalid-item>
      </warning>
    </entity-warning>
  </cbp-warnings>
</rejected>

  
The entity-type has the following valid values for the Entry Web Service -  
1\. ENTRY\_NUMBER - This will be used if the xml provides a entry number in the request  
2\. INVOICE\_NUMBER - This will be used if there is no entry number in xml and the error is in the invoice  
3\. HOUSE\_BILL - This will be used if there is no entry number in the xml and the issue is outside of the Invoice (i.e. invalid consignee)  
4\. NO\_ID - This will be used if there is no entry number in the request, the error is outside of the invoice, and there is no House bill  
\*\*\* If entity-type is ENTRY\_NUMBER, the entity-id will be {Filer Code}-{Entry Number}-{Check Digit} (i.e. ST9-1000001-1). \*\*\*  
Each Request could have multiple entity-warning tags if the entry number is not specified in request  
  
If there are problems, they will be in the following forms:

<rejected>username/password invalid</rejected>

<rejected>
    <validation-error>
        Line 31: cvc-complex-type.2.4.a: Invalid content was found starting with element
        'bad-tag'. One of '{"http://www.netchb.com/xml/entry":entry-no,
        "http://www.netchb.com/xml/entry":precalculated}' is expected.
    </validation-error>
</rejected>

<rejected>duplicate entry number</rejected>

<rejected>
    importer not found - an importer with tax id 11-12345678 must be in the user's importer table
</rejected>

<rejected>you do not have sufficient privileges</rejected>

<error><!-- A stack trace would be included here --></error>

			<xsd:element name="mode-transportation" type="data:modeTransportType" minOccurs="0" />
			<xsd:element name="unlading-port" type="data:portType" minOccurs="0" />
			<xsd:element name="import-date" type="xsd:date" minOccurs="0" />
			<xsd:element name="arrival-date" type="xsd:date" minOccurs="0" />
			<xsd:element name="paperless-summary-certification" minOccurs="0" />
			<!-- either certify-cargo-release tag will set the entry to be certified via ACE -->
			<xsd:element name="certify-cargo-release" minOccurs="0" />
			<xsd:element name="certify-cargo-release-via-ace" minOccurs="0" />
			<xsd:element name="not-to-be-certified" minOccurs="0" />
			<xsd:element name="carrier-code" type="data:carrierCodeType" minOccurs="0" />
			
			<xsd:element name="broker-reference-no" minOccurs="0">
				<xsd:simpleType>
					<xsd:restriction base="xsd:token">
						<xsd:maxLength value="9" />
					</xsd:restriction>
				</xsd:simpleType>
			</xsd:element>

			<xsd:element name="secondary-reference-no" minOccurs="0">
				<xsd:simpleType>
					<xsd:restriction base="xsd:token">
						<xsd:maxLength value="50" />
					</xsd:restriction>
				</xsd:simpleType>
			</xsd:element>
			
			<xsd:element name="customer-reference-no" minOccurs="0">
				<xsd:simpleType>
					<xsd:restriction base="xsd:token">
						<xsd:maxLength value="50" />
					</xsd:restriction>
				</xsd:simpleType>
			</xsd:element>
			
			<xsd:element name="voyage-no" minOccurs="0">
				<xsd:simpleType>
					<xsd:restriction base="xsd:token">
						<xsd:maxLength value="5" />
					</xsd:restriction>
				</xsd:simpleType>
			</xsd:element>
			
			<xsd:element name="location-of-goods" minOccurs="0">
				<xsd:simpleType>
					<xsd:restriction base="xsd:token">
						<xsd:maxLength value="4" />
					</xsd:restriction>
				</xsd:simpleType>
			</xsd:element>
			
			<xsd:element name="nafta-recon" minOccurs="0" />
			<xsd:element name="other-recon" type="entry:otherReconType" minOccurs="0" />
			
			<xsd:element name="bond-amount" minOccurs="0">
				<xsd:simpleType>
					<xsd:restriction base="xsd:token">
						<xsd:pattern value="\d{1,10}"/>
					</xsd:restriction>
				</xsd:simpleType>
			</xsd:element>
			
			<xsd:element name="bond-producer-account-no" minOccurs="0">
				<xsd:simpleType>
					<xsd:restriction base="xsd:token">
						<xsd:maxLength value="10" />
					</xsd:restriction>
				</xsd:simpleType>
			</xsd:element>
			
			<xsd:element name="warehouse-entry" minOccurs="0">
				<xsd:complexType>
					<xsd:all>
						<xsd:element name="warehouse-filer-code" type="data:filerCodeType" />
						<xsd:element name="warehouse-entry-no" type="data:entryNoType" />
						<xsd:element name="warehouse-port" type="data:portType" />
						<xsd:element name="final-withdrawal" minOccurs="0" />
					</xsd:all>
				</xsd:complexType>
			</xsd:element>
			
			<xsd:element name="general-order-no" minOccurs="0">
				<xsd:simpleType>
					<xsd:restriction base="xsd:token">
						<xsd:maxLength value="12" />
					</xsd:restriction>
				</xsd:simpleType>
			</xsd:element>
			
			<xsd:element name="trailer-no" minOccurs="0">
				<xsd:simpleType>
					<xsd:restriction base="xsd:token">
						<xsd:maxLength value="20" />
					</xsd:restriction>
				</xsd:simpleType>
			</xsd:element>
			
			<xsd:element name="person-in-charge" minOccurs="0">
				<xsd:simpleType>
					<xsd:restriction base="xsd:token">
						<xsd:maxLength value="30" />
					</xsd:restriction>
				</xsd:simpleType>
			</xsd:element>
			
			<xsd:element name="box1" minOccurs="0">
				<xsd:simpleType>
					<xsd:restriction base="xsd:token">
						<xsd:maxLength value="50" />
					</xsd:restriction>
				</xsd:simpleType>
			</xsd:element>
			
			<xsd:element name="box4" minOccurs="0">
				<xsd:simpleType>
					<xsd:restriction base="xsd:token">
						<xsd:maxLength value="250" />
					</xsd:restriction>
				</xsd:simpleType>
			</xsd:element>
			
			<xsd:element name="perishable" minOccurs="0"/>
			
			<xsd:element name="immediate-delivery" minOccurs="0"/>
			
			<xsd:element name="team-no" type="entry:teamNoType" minOccurs="0" />
			<xsd:element name="informal-fee" type="entry:classCodeAmountType" minOccurs="0" />
			<xsd:element name="mail-fee" type="entry:classCodeAmountType" minOccurs="0" />
			<xsd:element name="manual-surcharge" type="entry:classCodeAmountType" minOccurs="0" />
			
			<xsd:element name="consolidated-informal-indicator" minOccurs="0">
				<xsd:simpleType>
					<xsd:restriction base="xsd:token">
						<xsd:enumeration value="C" />
						<xsd:enumeration value="P" />
						<xsd:enumeration value="X" />
					</xsd:restriction>
				</xsd:simpleType>
			</xsd:element>
			
			<xsd:element name="freight-forwarder-name" minOccurs="0">
				<xsd:complexType>
				<xsd:choice>
					<xsd:element name="freight-forwarder-profile-name">
						<xsd:simpleType>
							<xsd:restriction base="xsd:token">
								<xsd:maxLength value="30" />
							</xsd:restriction>
						</xsd:simpleType>
					</xsd:element>
					<xsd:element name="freight-forwarder-company-name">
						<xsd:simpleType>
							<xsd:restriction base="xsd:token">
								<xsd:maxLength value="150" />
							</xsd:restriction>
						</xsd:simpleType>
					</xsd:element>
				</xsd:choice>
				</xsd:complexType>
			</xsd:element>
			
			<xsd:element name="bond-waiver-reason" minOccurs="0">
				<xsd:annotation>
					<xsd:documentation>
						This is an ACE element that should be included if the bond type is 00.
						995 - Supplemental Duty Bills on Vessel Repair Entries
						996 - Fines, Penalty, or Liquidated Damage Bills
						997 - All Other Contingent Bills
						998 - Bills Secured - Other than Surety
						999 - No Surety, Unsecured Bills
					</xsd:documentation>
				</xsd:annotation>
				<xsd:simpleType>
					<xsd:restriction base="xsd:token">
						<xsd:enumeration value="995"/>
						<xsd:enumeration value="996"/>
						<xsd:enumeration value="997"/>
						<xsd:enumeration value="998"/>
						<xsd:enumeration value="999"/>
					</xsd:restriction>
				</xsd:simpleType>
			</xsd:element>
			
			<xsd:element name="lloyds-vessel-code" minOccurs="0">
				<xsd:simpleType>
					<xsd:restriction base="xsd:token">
						<xsd:maxLength value="7"/>
					</xsd:restriction>
				</xsd:simpleType>
			</xsd:element>
			
			<xsd:element name="entry-date-election-code" minOccurs="0">
				<xsd:annotation>
					<xsd:documentation>
						P - Presentation Date
						A - Arrival Date
						W - Weekly Entry
					</xsd:documentation>
				</xsd:annotation>
				<xsd:simpleType>
					<xsd:restriction base="xsd:token">
						<xsd:enumeration value="P"/>
						<xsd:enumeration value="A"/>
						<xsd:enumeration value="W"/>
					</xsd:restriction>
				</xsd:simpleType>
			</xsd:element>

			<xsd:element name="presentation-date" minOccurs="0" type="xsd:date"/>

			<xsd:element name="superseded-bond" minOccurs="0">
				<xsd:annotation>
					<xsd:documentation>
						Including this tag, even if empty means superseded-bond is "Yes."  Only relevant if the bond type is 08
					</xsd:documentation>
				</xsd:annotation>
			</xsd:element>
			
			<xsd:element name="add-cvd-bond-type" type="entry:bondType" minOccurs="0"/>
			
			<xsd:element name="add-cvd-superseded-bond" minOccurs="0">
				<xsd:annotation>
					<xsd:documentation>
						Including this tag, even if empty means add-cvd-superseded-bond is "Yes."  Only relevant if the add/cvd bond type is 08
					</xsd:documentation>
				</xsd:annotation>
			</xsd:element>
			
			<xsd:element name="add-cvd-stb-amount" minOccurs="0">
				<xsd:simpleType>
					<xsd:restriction base="xsd:long">
						<xsd:minInclusive value="0"/>
						<xsd:maxInclusive value="9999999999"/>
					</xsd:restriction>
				</xsd:simpleType>
			</xsd:element>
			
			<xsd:element name="add-cvd-bond-producer-account-no" minOccurs="0">
				<xsd:simpleType>
					<xsd:restriction base="xsd:token">
						<xsd:maxLength value="10"/>
					</xsd:restriction>
				</xsd:simpleType>
			</xsd:element>
			
			<xsd:element name="post-summary-correction" minOccurs="0">
				<xsd:annotation>
					<xsd:documentation>
						If this tag is included that means post summary correction is "Yes".  This tag should be omitted in
						most circumstances.
					</xsd:documentation>
				</xsd:annotation>
				<xsd:complexType>
					<xsd:sequence>
						<xsd:element name="request-accelerated-liquidation" minOccurs="0" type="xsd:boolean">
							<xsd:annotation>
								<xsd:documentation>
									If this tag is not present, the value will be pulled from the Account -> Preferences -> Entry Defults page.
								</xsd:documentation>
							</xsd:annotation>
						</xsd:element>
						<xsd:element name="explanation-for-correction" minOccurs="1">
							<xsd:simpleType>
								<xsd:restriction base="xsd:token">
									<xsd:maxLength value="75"/>
								</xsd:restriction>
							</xsd:simpleType>
						</xsd:element>
						<xsd:element name="original-entry-no" minOccurs="0">
							<xsd:annotation>
								<xsd:documentation>
									Format should be either AAA-NNNNNNN-N or AAANNNNNNNN. 
								</xsd:documentation>
							</xsd:annotation>
						</xsd:element>
						<xsd:element name="psc-header-reason-code" minOccurs="0" maxOccurs="5">
							<xsd:annotation>
								<xsd:documentation>
									The reason codes are:
									H01 - Entry Type Change From 01 to 03
									H02 - Entry Type Changed to Other Type
									H04 - MOT Changed
									H05 - Surety Code Changed
									H06 - Superseded Bond Indicator Changed
									H07 - Other Bond Information Changed
									H08 - Electronic Invoice Indicator Changed
									H09 - Shipment Usage Type Changed
									H10 - Consignee Changed
									H11 - Import Date Changed
									H12 - State of Destination Changed
									H13 - Header Fee Changed
									H99 - Other Information Changed
								</xsd:documentation>
							</xsd:annotation>
							<xsd:simpleType>
								<xsd:restriction base="xsd:token">
									<xsd:enumeration value="H01"/>
									<xsd:enumeration value="H02"/>
									<xsd:enumeration value="H04"/>
									<xsd:enumeration value="H05"/>
									<xsd:enumeration value="H06"/>
									<xsd:enumeration value="H07"/>
									<xsd:enumeration value="H08"/>
									<xsd:enumeration value="H09"/>
									<xsd:enumeration value="H10"/>
									<xsd:enumeration value="H11"/>
									<xsd:enumeration value="H12"/>
									<xsd:enumeration value="H13"/>
									<xsd:enumeration value="H99"/>
								</xsd:restriction>
							</xsd:simpleType>
						</xsd:element>
					</xsd:sequence>
				</xsd:complexType>
			</xsd:element>
		</xsd:all>
	</xsd:complexType>
	
	<!-- **************************************************************** -->
	<xsd:complexType name="consolidatedEntryType">
		<xsd:annotation>
			<xsd:documentation>
				The consolidated entry type is for information that should be
				included if 
			</xsd:documentation>
		</xsd:annotation>
		<xsd:sequence>
			<xsd:element name="total-manifest-quantity">
				<xsd:simpleType>
					<xsd:restriction base="xsd:token">
						<xsd:pattern value="\d{1,10}" />
					</xsd:restriction>
				</xsd:simpleType>
			</xsd:element>
			<xsd:element name="consolidated-entry" minOccurs="1" maxOccurs="unbounded">
				<xsd:complexType>
					<xsd:all>
						<xsd:element name="filer-code" type="data:filerCodeType" />
						<xsd:element name="entry-no" type="data:entryNoType" />
					</xsd:all>
				</xsd:complexType>
			</xsd:element>
		</xsd:sequence>
	</xsd:complexType>

	<!-- **************************************************************** -->
	<xsd:complexType name="containerType">
		<xsd:all>
			<xsd:element name="container-number" type="xsd:string" minOccurs="0"/>
			<xsd:element name="container-size" minOccurs="0">
				<xsd:simpleType>
					<xsd:restriction base="xsd:string">
						<xsd:enumeration value="20 ft"/>
						<xsd:enumeration value="20 ft HC"/>
						<xsd:enumeration value="40 ft"/>
						<xsd:enumeration value="40 ft HC"/>
						<xsd:enumeration value="45 ft"/>
						<xsd:enumeration value="45 ft HC"/>
						<xsd:enumeration value="53 ft"/>
						<xsd:enumeration value="53 ft HC"/>
					</xsd:restriction>
				</xsd:simpleType>
			</xsd:element>
			<xsd:element name="container-type" minOccurs="0">
				<xsd:simpleType>
					<xsd:restriction base="xsd:string">
						<xsd:enumeration value="Dry"/>
						<xsd:enumeration value="Flat Rack"/>
						<xsd:enumeration value="Headload"/>
						<xsd:enumeration value="Open"/>
						<xsd:enumeration value="Reefer"/>
						<xsd:enumeration value="LCL"/>
						<xsd:enumeration value="Tank"/>
					</xsd:restriction>
				</xsd:simpleType>
			</xsd:element>
			<xsd:element name="seal-numbers" type="xsd:string" minOccurs="0"/>
			<xsd:element name="po-number" type="xsd:string" minOccurs="0"/>
			<xsd:element name="po-number-descriptor" minOccurs="0"/>
			<xsd:element name="weight" type="xsd:double" minOccurs="0"/>
			<xsd:element name="weight-unit" minOccurs="0">
				<xsd:simpleType>
					<xsd:restriction base="xsd:string">
						<xsd:enumeration value="KG"/>
						<xsd:enumeration value="LB"/>
					</xsd:restriction>
				</xsd:simpleType>
			</xsd:element>
			<xsd:element name="quantity" type="xsd:double" minOccurs="0"/>
			<xsd:element name="quantity-unit" minOccurs="0">
				<xsd:simpleType>
					<xsd:restriction base="xsd:token">
						<xsd:maxLength value="30"/>
					</xsd:restriction>
				</xsd:simpleType>
			</xsd:element>
		</xsd:all>
	</xsd:complexType>

	<!-- **************************************************************** -->
	<xsd:complexType name="manifestType">
		<xsd:annotation>
			<xsd:documentation>
				This is the element type that contains manifest information
			</xsd:documentation>
		</xsd:annotation>
		<xsd:sequence>
			<xsd:element name="inbond-date" type="xsd:date" minOccurs="0" />
			
			<xsd:element name="split-shipment" minOccurs="0">
				<xsd:annotation>
					<xsd:documentation>
						For Air shipments via ACE, split-shipment can be included to note
						this is a split shipment.
						1 - Hold entire shipment until all is released
						2 - Request Permit to release cargo incrementally under Immediate Delivery
					</xsd:documentation>
				</xsd:annotation>
				<xsd:simpleType>
					<xsd:restriction base="xsd:token">
						<xsd:enumeration value="1"/>
						<xsd:enumeration value="2"/>
					</xsd:restriction>
				</xsd:simpleType>
			</xsd:element>
			
			<xsd:element name="bill-of-lading" minOccurs="0" maxOccurs="unbounded">
				<xsd:complexType>
					<xsd:all>
						<xsd:element name="inbond-no" minOccurs="0" type="data:inbondNoType" />
						<xsd:element name="master-scac" minOccurs="0" type="data:carrierCodeType" />
						<xsd:element name="master-bill" minOccurs="0" type="data:billNoType" />
						<xsd:element name="house-scac" minOccurs="0" type="data:carrierCodeType" />
						<xsd:element name="house-bill" minOccurs="0" type="data:billNoType" />
						<xsd:element name="sub-house-bill" minOccurs="0" type="data:billNoType" />
						<xsd:element name="quantity">
							<xsd:simpleType>
								<xsd:restriction base="xsd:integer">
									<xsd:minInclusive value="0"/>
								</xsd:restriction>
							</xsd:simpleType>
						</xsd:element>
						<xsd:element name="unit">
							<xsd:simpleType>
								<xsd:restriction base="xsd:token">
									<xsd:maxLength value="5"/>
								</xsd:restriction>
							</xsd:simpleType>
						</xsd:element>
						
						<xsd:element name="split-shipments" minOccurs="0">
							<xsd:complexType>
								<xsd:sequence>
									<xsd:element name="split-shipment" type="entry:splitShipmentType" minOccurs="0" maxOccurs="unbounded"/>
								</xsd:sequence>
							</xsd:complexType>
						</xsd:element>
					</xsd:all>
				</xsd:complexType>
			</xsd:element>
			
			<xsd:element name="exam-site" minOccurs="0">
				<xsd:simpleType>
					<xsd:restriction base="xsd:token">
						<xsd:maxLength value="40"/>
					</xsd:restriction>
				</xsd:simpleType>
			</xsd:element>
		</xsd:sequence>
	</xsd:complexType>
	
	<!-- **************************************************************** -->
	<xsd:complexType name="splitShipmentType">
		<xsd:annotation>
			<xsd:documentation>
				This is used to include the split shipment information for a given bill of lading
			</xsd:documentation>
		</xsd:annotation>
		<xsd:all>
			<xsd:element name="carrier" type="data:carrierCodeType"/>
			<xsd:element name="flight-no">
				<xsd:simpleType>
					<xsd:restriction base="xsd:token">
						<xsd:maxLength value="5"/>
					</xsd:restriction>
				</xsd:simpleType>
			</xsd:element>
			<xsd:element name="arrival-date" type="xsd:date"/>
			<xsd:element name="quantity">
				<xsd:simpleType>
					<xsd:restriction base="xsd:integer">
						<xsd:minInclusive value="0"/>
						<xsd:maxInclusive value="99999999"/>
					</xsd:restriction>
				</xsd:simpleType>
			</xsd:element>
		</xsd:all>
	</xsd:complexType>

	<!-- **************************************************************** -->
	<xsd:complexType name="invoiceType">
		<xsd:annotation>
			<xsd:documentation>
				This is the element that contains invoice information for each
				invoice listed on the entry
			</xsd:documentation>
		</xsd:annotation>
		<xsd:all>
			<xsd:element name="invoice-no" type="data:invoiceNoType" />

			<xsd:element name="aii-supplier-id" type="data:manufacturerIdType" minOccurs="0">
				<xsd:annotation>
					<xsd:documentation>
						This should be included if the electronic-invoice tag is present
						in the entry header
					</xsd:documentation>
				</xsd:annotation>
			</xsd:element>

			<xsd:element name="ultimate-consignee-tax-id" type="data:taxIdType" minOccurs="0">
				<xsd:annotation>
					<xsd:documentation>
						ultimate-consignee-info or ultimate-consignee-tax-id should be included if the multiple tag was chosen for the
						ultimate-consignee in the entry header
					</xsd:documentation>
				</xsd:annotation>
			</xsd:element>

			<xsd:element name="ultimate-consignee-info" minOccurs="0">
				<xsd:annotation>
					<xsd:documentation>
						ultimate-consignee-info or ultimate-consignee-tax-id should be included if the multiple tag was chosen for the
						ultimate-consignee in the entry header.
					</xsd:documentation>
				</xsd:annotation>
				<xsd:complexType>
					<xsd:all>
						<xsd:element name="consignee-name" minOccurs="1">
							<xsd:simpleType>
								<xsd:restriction base="xsd:token">
									<xsd:maxLength value="100"/>
								</xsd:restriction>
							</xsd:simpleType>
						</xsd:element>
						<xsd:element name="consignee-address1" minOccurs="1">
							<xsd:simpleType>
								<xsd:restriction base="xsd:token">
									<xsd:maxLength value="100"/>
								</xsd:restriction>
							</xsd:simpleType>
						</xsd:element>
						<xsd:element name="consignee-address2" minOccurs="0">
							<xsd:simpleType>
								<xsd:restriction base="xsd:token">
									<xsd:maxLength value="100"/>
								</xsd:restriction>
							</xsd:simpleType>
						</xsd:element>
						<xsd:element name="consignee-city" minOccurs="1">
							<xsd:simpleType>
								<xsd:restriction base="xsd:token">
									<xsd:maxLength value="100"/>
								</xsd:restriction>
							</xsd:simpleType>
						</xsd:element>
						<xsd:element name="consignee-state" minOccurs="1">
							<xsd:simpleType>
								<xsd:restriction base="xsd:token">
									<xsd:maxLength value="2"/>
								</xsd:restriction>
							</xsd:simpleType>
						</xsd:element>
						<xsd:element name="consignee-zip" minOccurs="1">
							<xsd:simpleType>
								<xsd:restriction base="xsd:token">
									<xsd:maxLength value="40"/>
								</xsd:restriction>
							</xsd:simpleType>
						</xsd:element>
					</xsd:all>
				</xsd:complexType>
			</xsd:element>

			<xsd:element name="related-party" minOccurs="0" />

			<xsd:element name="foreign-currency" minOccurs="0">
				<xsd:annotation>
					<xsd:documentation>
						Include the foreign-currency element if the invoice is in a currency that is not USD.
						If currency-code and currency-country-code are given, but exchange-rate is not, the system
						will auto-populate the exchange rate based on the currency-code, currency-country-code and export date
					</xsd:documentation>
				</xsd:annotation>
				<xsd:complexType>
					<xsd:all>
						<xsd:element name="currency-code" minOccurs="1">
							<xsd:simpleType>
								<xsd:restriction base="xsd:token">
									<xsd:pattern value="[A-Z]{3}"/>
								</xsd:restriction>
							</xsd:simpleType>
						</xsd:element>
						<xsd:element name="exchange-rate" minOccurs="0">
							<xsd:simpleType>
								<xsd:restriction base="xsd:float">
									<xsd:minExclusive value="0"/>
								</xsd:restriction>
							</xsd:simpleType>
						</xsd:element>
						<xsd:element name="currency-country-code" minOccurs="0">
							<xsd:simpleType>
								<xsd:restriction base="xsd:token">
									<xsd:pattern value="[A-Z]{2}"/>
								</xsd:restriction>
							</xsd:simpleType>
						</xsd:element>
					</xsd:all>
				</xsd:complexType>
			</xsd:element>
			
			<xsd:element name="proration-amount" minOccurs="0">
				<xsd:simpleType>
					<xsd:restriction base="xsd:decimal">
						<xsd:fractionDigits value="2"/>
					</xsd:restriction>
				</xsd:simpleType>
			</xsd:element>
			
			<xsd:element name="precalculated-prorated-lines" minOccurs="0">
				<xsd:annotation>
					<xsd:documentation>
						<![CDATA[
							This should be included if the line item values have already been prorated and the system should not prorate the invoice lines again.
							If you choose to use this tag, the value-adjustment tags in the tariff section need to add up to the amount of proration that was removed from each line.
						]]>
					</xsd:documentation>
				</xsd:annotation>

```ts
// Port and country code resolution for NetCHB XML.
// NetCHB entry-port and processing-port use 4-digit CBP port codes (Schedule D).
// Country of origin uses ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 codes.

const usPortCodes: Record<string,string> = {
  tacoma: '3002',
  seattle: '3001',
  portland: '3004',
  // ...
}
const countryCodes: Record<string,string> = {
  vietnam: 'VN', bangladesh: 'BD', china: 'CN', ...
}

export function resolvePortCode(value: string | null): string | null {
  if (!value) return null
  const trimmed = value.trim()
  if (/^\d{4}$/.test(trimmed)) return trimmed
  return usPortCodes[trimmed.toLowerCase()] ?? null
}

export function resolveCountryCode(value: string | null): string | null {
  if (!value) return null
  const trimmed = value.trim()
  if (/^[A-Za-z]{2}$/.test(trimmed)) return trimmed.toUpperCase()
  return countryCodes[trimmed.toLowerCase()] ?? null
}

export function resolveBondType(value: string | null): string | null {
  if (!value) return null
  const trimmed = value.trim()
  if (/^(00|08|09)$/.test(trimmed)) return trimmed
  const label = trimmed.toLowerCase()
  if (label.includes('continuous')) return '08'
  if (label.includes('single')) return '09'
  if (label.includes('no bond') || label.includes('unsecured')) return '00'
  return null
}
```

```ts
// NetCHB code normalization.
//
// The NetCHB entry XSD requires machine codes, while extracted documents and
// the review UI use human-readable values:
//   - processing-port / entry-port: 4-digit CBP port codes (CBP Schedule D)
//   - country-origin: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2
//   - bond-type: XSD enumeration 00, 08, 09
// Normalization happens only when rendering XML; the UI keeps the document text.

const usPortCodes: Record<string, string> = {
  // Source: CBP Schedule D. Intentionally small and explicit - add verified
  // entries only. Unmapped ports are reported as errors rather than guessed.
  tacoma: '3002',
}

const countryCodes: Record<string, string> = {
  vietnam: 'VN',
  bangladesh: 'BD',
  ...
}

const bondTypes: Record<string, string> = {
  '00': '00',
  '08': '08',
  '09': '09',
  'no bond': '00',
  unsecured: '00',
  continuous: '08',
  'continuous bond': '08',
  single: '09',
  'single transaction': '09',
  'single entry': '09',
}

export function resolvePortCode(value: string | null): string | null {
  if (!value) return null
  const trimmed = value.trim()
  if (/^\d{4}$/.test(trimmed)) return trimmed
  return usPortCodes[trimmed.toLowerCase()] ?? null
}

export function resolveCountryCode(value: string | null): string | null {
  if (!value) return null
  const trimmed = value.trim()
  if (/^[A-Za-z]{2}$/.test(trimmed)) return trimmed.toUpperCase()
  return countryCodes[trimmed.toLowerCase()] ?? null
}

export function resolveBondType(value: string | null): string | null {
  if (!value) return null
  const trimmed = value.trim()
  if (/^(00|08|09)$/.test(trimmed)) return trimmed
  return bondTypes[trimmed.toLowerCase()] ?? null
}
```

```ts
import { resolveBondType, resolveCountryCode, resolvePortCode } from './netchb-codes.js'

  return typeof value === 'object' && value !== null && 'value' in value ? (value as { value: string | number | null }).value : null
}

function missingRequiredFields(shipment: Shipment): string[] {
  return requiredShipmentFields.filter((path) => valueOf(path.split('.').reduce<unknown>((current, key) => (current as Record<string, unknown>)?.[key], shipment)) == null)
}

function escapeXml(...) {...}
function element(...) {...}

function foreignPort(value) { return value && /^\d{5}$/.test(value) ? value : null }

export function renderNetchbXml(shipment: Shipment): RenderResult {
  const errors = new Set(missingRequiredFields(shipment))

  const processingPort = resolvePortCode(shipment.transport.processingPort.value)
  const entryPort = resolvePortCode(shipment.transport.entryPort.value)
  const dischargePort = resolvePortCode(shipment.transport.dischargePort.value)
  const bondType = resolveBondType(shipment.entry.bondType.value)
  const countryCodes = shipment.lines.map((line) => resolveCountryCode(line.countryOfOrigin.value))

  // Required codes must resolve; never emit a guessed or non-conforming value.
  if (!processingPort) errors.add('transport.processingPort')
  if (!entryPort) errors.add('transport.entryPort')
  if (!bondType) errors.add('entry.bondType')
  shipment.lines.forEach((_, index) => { if (!countryCodes[index]) errors.add(`lines.${index}.countryOfOrigin`) })
  shipment.lines.forEach((line, index) => {
    if (line.value.value == null) errors.add(`lines.${index}.value`)
    if (line.htsCode.value == null) errors.add(`lines.${index}.htsCode`)
  })

  if (errors.size) return { errors: [...errors] }
  ...
}
```

```ts
export function detectConflicts(observations: Observation[]): Conflict[] {
  const groups = new Map<string, Map<string, {raw: string; documents: Set<string>}>>()
  for (const obs of observations) {
    const kind = identifierKindForField(obs.field)
    const normalized = normalizeValue(obs.value, kind)
    if (!normalized) continue
    const byValue = groups.get(obs.field) ?? new Map()
    groups.set(obs.field, byValue)
    const entry = byValue.get(normalized) ?? { raw: obs.value.trim(), documents: new Set<string>() }
    entry.documents.add(obs.document)
    byValue.set(normalized, entry)
  }
  const conflicts: Conflict[] = []
  for (const [field, byValue] of groups) {
    if (byValue.size < 2) continue
    conflicts.push({ field, values: [...byValue.values()].map((v) => v.raw) })
  }
  return conflicts
}
```

```ts
}
```

```ts
export function normalizeDate(value: string): string {
  const trimmed = value.trim()
```

```ts
export function isIsoDate(value: string): boolean {
  const m = /^(\d{4})-(\d{2})-(\d{2})$/.exec(value)
```

Done.

Added a deterministic guard so a foreign port can never land in a U.S. port field.

- `src/lib/sanitize.ts` — `sanitizeTransportPorts` checks `processingPort`, `entryPort`, and `dischargePort`. If the value resolves as a foreign port (Schedule K) but not as a U.S. port, it clears the field, sets confidence to 0, and adds a review flag: *"Processing port must be a U.S. CBP port, but the document provided the foreign port 'CAT LAI, HCMC, VN'. Enter the correct 4-digit CBP port."*
- `src/lib/extraction.ts` — runs the sanitizer after parsing (server-side).
- `src/app.ts` — runs it again after extraction so the client state matches, and the flag shows in the Review notes panel.

So now when the model misplaces `CAT LAI, HCMC, VN` into Processing port, the field becomes empty (Missing) with a clear note, and you enter the real U.S. port (e.g. Tacoma → 3002) instead of the app trying to use the foreign port.

# Cline SDK

> TypeScript packages for embedding Cline's agent runtime in your own applications.

The Cline SDK is an open source framework for building agentic applications, and is the same harness used in the Cline IDE extensions and CLI. It uses a plugin architecture that makes it easy to customize and comes with all the features you expect from agents like checkpoints, web fetch, MCPs, cron jobs, subagents, and more.

Use the Cline SDK to run agents from CI/CD pipelines, create automations for end-to-end workflows, or embed agents directly inside your products.

## Install

```bash theme={"system"}
npm install @cline/sdk
```

`@cline/sdk` exports all SDK packages: `@cline/core` for the full agent harness, `@cline/agents` for the stateless agent loop, `@cline/llms` for control over the model gateway, and `@cline/shared` for common utilities.

Requires Node.js 22 or later.

## SDK Skill

If you use a coding agent (Claude Code, Codex, Cline, etc.), install the [Cline SDK skill](https://github.com/cline/sdk-skill) to give your agent context on the SDK's APIs and best practices to help you build with the Cline SDK.

```bash theme={"system"}
npx skills add cline/sdk-skill
```

Prompt it to scaffold agents, create custom tools, wire up plugins, configure providers, and more.

## Your First Agent

```typescript theme={"system"}
import { Agent } from "@cline/sdk"

const agent = new Agent({
  providerId: "anthropic",
  modelId: "claude-sonnet-4-6",
  apiKey: process.env.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY,
  maxIterations: 1,
})

agent.subscribe((event) => {
  if (event.type === "assistant-text-delta") {
    process.stdout.write(event.text ?? "")
  }
})

const result = await agent.run("Explain what an SDK is in two sentences.")
```

# Building an Agent

> Walk through a complete code review bot that reads diffs, analyzes code, and produces structured feedback.

This tutorial walks through the [code-review-bot example](https://github.com/cline/cline/tree/main/apps/examples/code-review-bot) from the SDK repository. By the end, you'll understand how to combine custom tools, system prompts, completion lifecycle, and event streaming into a real application.

## What It Builds

A code review agent that:

1. Reads a git diff from the local repo
2. Optionally reads full file contents for context
3. Produces structured review comments with severity levels
4. Ends the run with a summary and approve/reject decision

## Prerequisites

* Node.js 22+
* An Anthropic API key
* A git repository with at least one commit

## Get the Code

```bash theme={"system"}
git clone https://github.com/cline/cline.git
cd cline/apps/examples/code-review-bot
bun install
```

Or read along with the [source on GitHub](https://github.com/cline/cline/blob/main/apps/examples/code-review-bot/src/index.ts).

## How It Works

### Defining Tools with Zod Schemas

The bot uses `createTool` with zod schemas for type-safe tool definitions. Here's the review comment tool:

```typescript theme={"system"}
createTool({
  name: "add_review_comment",
  description: "Add a review comment on a specific file and line.",
  inputSchema: z.object({
    file: z.string().describe("File path"),
    line: z.number().describe("Line number (approximate is fine)"),
    severity: z.enum(["critical", "warning", "suggestion"]),
    comment: z.string().describe("The review comment"),
  }),
  async execute(input) {
    reviews.push(input)
    return `Comment added (${reviews.length} total)`
  },
})
```

Key points:

* `z.enum` constrains severity to valid values, which improves model accuracy
* `.describe()` on each field tells the model what to provide
* The tool accumulates results in an array for post-run processing

### Completion Tools

The `submit_review` tool uses `lifecycle: { completesRun: true }` to signal that the agent's work is done:

```typescript theme={"system"}
createTool({
  name: "submit_review",
  description: "Submit the completed review with a summary.",
  inputSchema: z.object({
    summary: z.string().describe("Brief overall assessment of the changes"),
    approve: z.boolean().describe("Whether the changes look good to merge"),
  }),
  lifecycle: { completesRun: true },
  async execute(input) {
    return JSON.stringify({ summary: input.summary, approve: input.approve })
  },
})
```

Without this, the agent would keep looping until `maxIterations`. With it, the agent calls `submit_review` when it's done and the run ends cleanly.

### System Prompt

The system prompt gives the agent a structured workflow to follow:

```typescript theme={"system"}
const agent = new Agent({
  systemPrompt: `You are a senior code reviewer. Analyze the git diff provided and leave review comments using the add_review_comment tool. Focus on:
- Bugs and logic errors (critical)
- Security issues (critical)
- Performance problems (warning)
- Style and readability improvements (suggestion)

When you are done reviewing, call submit_review with a brief summary.`,
  // ...
})
```

Telling the agent exactly which tools to use and when keeps the workflow predictable.

### Event Streaming

The bot subscribes to events to show progress as the agent works:

```typescript theme={"system"}
agent.subscribe((event) => {
  switch (event.type) {
    case "assistant-text-delta":
      process.stdout.write(event.text ?? "")
      break
    case "tool-started":
      if (event.toolCall.toolName === "add_review_comment") {
        const input = event.toolCall.input
        console.log(`  [${input.severity}] ${input.file}:${input.line} - ${input.comment}`)
      }
      break
  }
})
```

This prints review comments as they're made, so you see results streaming rather than waiting for the full run to finish.

### Post-Run Processing

After the run, the bot groups comments by severity and prints a summary:

```typescript theme={"system"}
const result = await agent.run(`Review this git diff:\n\n\`\`\`diff\n${diff}\n\`\`\``)

const critical = reviews.filter((r) => r.severity === "critical")
const warnings = reviews.filter((r) => r.severity === "warning")
const suggestions = reviews.filter((r) => r.severity === "suggestion")
```

The tool calls accumulate structured data during the run, and the application processes it after. This pattern is useful any time you want the agent to produce structured output.

## Run It

```bash theme={"system"}
ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-... bun dev        # review last commit
ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-... bun dev main   # review against main
```

## Extending Further

From here, you could:

* Add a tool that posts review comments back to GitHub via the API
* Use `continue()` for follow-up questions about specific findings
* Add a `checkstyle` tool that runs linters on the changed files
* Connect it to a webhook for automatic PR reviews

## Understanding Port Codes

U.S. Customs and Border Protection maintains two official port code systems. **Schedule D** assigns numeric codes to domestic ports of entry — the 522 locations where goods may be formally entered for import into the United States. Each port belongs to a customs district and may have dozens of FIRMS facilities attached.

**Schedule K** covers foreign ports of lading and unlading — the 3,769 international locations from which goods originate or transit before arriving in the US. These codes appear on entry documents, bills of lading, and automated broker interface (ABI) transmissions.

Port codes matter because they determine which CBP Center of Excellence and Expertise (CEE) processes your entry, which FIRMS facilities you can use, and in some cases, which rulings and regulations apply. Knowing the correct port code prevents delays, penalties, and misdirected cargo.

## What are Schedule D Port Codes?

Schedule D port codes are the official numeric identifiers that U.S. Customs and Border Protection assigns to every domestic port of entry. Each code consists of a four-digit number where the first two digits indicate the customs district and the remaining digits identify the specific port within that district. Importers, brokers, and carriers must cite the correct Schedule D code on every customs entry, in-bond movement, and warehouse withdrawal filed with CBP.

Getting the port code wrong can route your entry to the wrong Center of Excellence and Expertise, delay cargo release, or trigger penalties. The district-port hierarchy also determines which FIRMS facilities (container freight stations, bonded warehouses, and Foreign Trade Zones) are available for examination and storage. When planning an import, always verify the Schedule D code against the port where goods will physically arrive and be presented to CBP.

32: - A bill-of-lading or invoice "Type of Move", "Service Type", "CFS / DOOR", "CY/CY", "Door", "Port to Door" value is not entry.type. entry.type is the 2-digit CBP entry type code (for example 01 = consumption). Use null unless that code is stated.

Done. Focused on `transport.entryPort` and `transport.processingPort`.

## What the NetCHB fields actually mean (from the XSD + NetCHB docs)

- `processing-port` — `data:portType` (`\d{4}`). The 4-digit **CBP Schedule D** code for the port associated with the filer's *account* where the entry is processed. NetCHB's own response documentation warns *"The Preparer Port Should match the Account Processing Port."* It is an account-level value, not a foreign port, and is usually not printed on shipping documents.
- `entry-port` — `data:portType` (`\d{4}`). The 4-digit **CBP Schedule D** code for the U.S. port of entry.
- Related roles: `unlading-port` = 4-digit Schedule D U.S. port of discharge; `lading-port` (line) = 5-digit **Schedule K** foreign port of loading.

```ts
export function validateArithmetic(shipment: Shipment): ArithmeticIssue[] {
  const issues: ArithmeticIssue[] = []
  const decimals = currencyDecimals(shipment.invoice.currency.value)
  const isExcluded = (line) => line.freeOfCharge?.value === true || line.value.value === 0

  shipment.lines.forEach((line, index) => {
    const qty = line.quantity.value
    const unitPrice = line.unitPrice?.value ?? null
    const stated = line.value.value
    if (isExcluded(line)) return
    if (qty == null || unitPrice == null || stated == null) {
      issues.push({ path: `lines.${index}.value`, kind: 'missing-input', expected: null, stated, difference: null, message: `Cannot verify line ${index+1}: ${missingParts} missing.`, evidence: source, severity: 'warning' })
      return
    }
    const expected = roundTo(qty * unitPrice, decimals)
    const statedRounded = roundTo(stated, decimals)
    if (expected !== statedRounded) {
      issues.push({ path: `lines.${index}.value`, kind: 'line-amount', expected, stated: statedRounded, difference: roundTo(statedRounded - expected, decimals), message: `Line ${index+1}: quantity × unit price = ${expected}, but the stated amount is ${statedRounded}.`, evidence, severity: 'warning' })
    }
  })

  // subtotal
  const activeLines = shipment.lines.filter((line) => !isExcluded(line))
  const subtotal = roundTo(activeLines.reduce((total, line) => total + (line.value.value ?? 0), 0), decimals)
  const declaredSubtotal = shipment.invoice.subtotal?.value ?? null
  if (declaredSubtotal != null && roundTo(declaredSubtotal, decimals) !== subtotal) {
    issues.push({ path: 'invoice.subtotal', kind: 'line-subtotal', expected: subtotal, stated: roundTo(declaredSubtotal, decimals), difference: ..., message: `Line items sum to ${subtotal}, but the invoice subtotal states ${...}.`, evidence })
  }
  const declaredTotal = shipment.invoice.total?.value ?? null
  if (declaredTotal != null) {
    const freight = shipment.totals.freight.value ?? 0
    const insurance = shipment.totals.insurance.value ?? 0
    const interpretations = [...new Set([subtotal, roundTo(subtotal+freight, decimals), roundTo(subtotal+insurance, decimals), roundTo(subtotal+freight+insurance, decimals)])]
    const statedTotal = roundTo(declaredTotal, decimals)
    if (!interpretations.includes(statedTotal)) {
      const expected = roundTo(subtotal + freight + insurance, decimals)
      issues.push({ path: 'invoice.total', kind: 'invoice-total', expected, stated: statedTotal, difference: ..., message: `Line items${freight||insurance ? ' plus freight/insurance' : ''} total ${expected}, but the invoice total states ${statedTotal}.`, evidence })
    }
  }
  return issues
}
```

```ts
export function validateArithmetic(shipment: Shipment): ArithmeticIssue[] {
  const issues: ArithmeticIssue[] = []
  const decimals = currencyDecimals(shipment.invoice.currency.value)
  const isExcluded = (line) => line.freeOfCharge?.value === true || line.value.value === 0

  shipment.lines.forEach((line, index) => {
    const qty = line.quantity.value
    const unitPrice = line.unitPrice?.value ?? null
    const stated = line.value.value
    if (isExcluded(line)) return
    if (qty == null || unitPrice == null || stated == null) {
      issues.push({ path: `lines.${index}.value`, kind: 'missing-input', expected: null, stated, difference: null, message: `Cannot verify line ${index+1}: ${missingParts} missing.`, evidence: source, severity: 'warning' })
      return
    }
    const expected = roundTo(qty * unitPrice, decimals)
    const statedRounded = roundTo(stated, decimals)
    if (expected !== statedRounded) {
      issues.push({ path: `lines.${index}.value`, kind: 'line-amount', expected, stated: statedRounded, difference: roundTo(statedRounded - expected, decimals), message: `Line ${index+1}: quantity × unit price = ${expected}, but the stated amount is ${statedRounded}.`, evidence, severity: 'warning' })
    }
  })

  // subtotal
  const activeLines = shipment.lines.filter((line) => !isExcluded(line))
  const subtotal = roundTo(activeLines.reduce((total, line) => total + (line.value.value ?? 0), 0), decimals)
  const declaredSubtotal = shipment.invoice.subtotal?.value ?? null
  if (declaredSubtotal != null && roundTo(declaredSubtotal, decimals) !== subtotal) {
```

content.text:
Implemented deterministic invoice arithmetic validation.

**New module — `src/lib/arithmetic.ts`** (pure, model-independent):
- `roundTo(value, decimals)` and `currencyDecimals(currency)` (ISO 4217; JPY/KRW/VND/etc. → 0 decimals, default 2).
- `isFreeOfCharge(line)` — explicit flag, zero unit price, or no unit price with a zero amount.
- `validateArithmetic(shipment)` returns issues of kind `line-amount`, `line-subtotal`, `invoice-total`, `missing-input`, each with `expected`, `stated`, `difference`, `message`, and `evidence` (source document/page). It never mutates the shipment (covered by a test).
- Line check: `quantity × unitPrice` rounded to currency precision vs the stated line amount.
- Subtotal: sum of non-excluded lines vs declared `invoice.subtotal`.
- Total: accepts any valid composition (subtotal, +freight, +insurance, +both) vs declared `invoice.total`; flags only when none match.
- Free samples are excluded from subtotal/total and skipped for the line-amount check.

**Schema (`src/lib/shipment.ts`)** — optional, backward-compatible additions: `line.unitPrice`, `line.freeOfCharge`, `invoice.subtotal`, `invoice.total`.

**UI (`src/app.ts`)**:
- Added editable "Unit price" per line and "Declared subtotal"/"Declared total" invoice fields.
- New **Arithmetic checks** panel showing each mismatch with expected, stated, difference, and source evidence.
- Recomputed on every render, so it runs right after extraction and on every relevant field edit.

**Extraction prompt** — asks for `unitPrice`, `invoice.subtotal`, and `invoice.total` exactly as printed (no computed values). No XML renderer changes.

**Tests — `tests/arithmetic.test.ts`** (11): matching amounts, mismatch, floating-point/rounding tolerance, JPY minor-unit rounding, missing inputs, all-missing skipped, free-of-charge exclusion, subtotal mismatch, total including freight/insurance, total with no valid composition, no-mutation, and `roundTo`.

Results: `pnpm test` → **14 files, 66 tests passing**; `pnpm build` clean.

Root cause found and fixed.

## Trace result

- **Extraction prompt** — requested `unitPrice`, `invoice.subtotal`, `invoice.total` but never `freeOfCharge`.
- **Model response schema** — `unitPrice`, `freeOfCharge`, `invoice.subtotal`, `invoice.total` were declared `.optional()`, so `z.toJSONSchema()` left them out of the schema's `required` array:
  - `lines.items.required` was `[description, countryOfOrigin, htsCode, quantity, unit, value]`
  - `invoice.required` was `[number, date, currency, incoterm]`
  - The model treats non-required properties as skippable and omitted them.
- **Parsing / normalization / state / UI bindings** — verified correct. A mocked `/api/extract` response containing the fields rendered `unitPrice=2.7`, `subtotal=6480`, `total=10515` in the form. So the gap was upstream: the model never emitted the values.

## Fix

- `src/lib/shipment.ts` — changed the four fields from `.optional()` to `.default({ value: null, confidence: 0 })`. Verified this puts them into the schema `required` list (`lines.items.required` and `invoice.required` now include them) and makes `parse` always produce the field (null when the model omits it), so the form and arithmetic module always have it.
- `src/lib/extraction.ts` — golden rule now states every property must be present (null when unstated), and the Amounts instruction now defines `freeOfCharge`.
- `src/app.ts` — unchanged; `ensureReviewShipment` remains a harmless safety net.

No hardcoded sample values; the fix is generic to the schema.

## Tests

Added `tests/extraction-schema.test.ts`: the model schema requires the arithmetic fields, parse fills null defaults when omitted, and extracted values survive parsing.
